title: Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour
subtitle: Camelot · GameCube

body: Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour is Camelot's GameCube golf game, combining Mario characters with courses that move from recognisable fairways toward more fantastical Mushroom Kingdom terrain. The aim remains to finish each hole in as few strokes as possible. Character statistics influence power, control and the height of a shot, making the selection of golfer part of the approach. The player studies distance, wind and the landing area before using a timed power meter to turn that plan into a particular stroke.

Later courses introduce features such as Chain Chomps, lava and pipes, placing Mario's world inside the practical problem of finding a safe route to the hole. Spin changes how a ball behaves after landing, while automatic and manual shots offer different balances of assistance and risk. A useful stroke is therefore more than a successful timing input. The ball must arrive somewhere that leaves the next attempt manageable, and a stronger shot can be less valuable than a carefully chosen position on a difficult green.

Ring Attack adds hoops to pass through while meeting a score requirement, asking the player to reconsider the familiar layout. Character matches and tournaments open further rewards, while connection with Mario Golf: Advance Tour links the home-console game to its Game Boy Advance companion. Motoi Sakuraba composed the music. Released in 2003, Toadstool Tour builds its variety through the relationship between a consistent swing system and increasingly expressive courses. Learning the controls creates a foundation; reading what a particular hole asks of those controls supplies the continuing game.
